# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM **MGE Niagara Entertainment Inc. - Fourth Amended and Restated Limited Waiver** --- ## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY **Date of Agreement:** September 30, 2020 **Borrower:** MGE Niagara Entertainment Inc., a casino operations company **Transaction Overview:** This Fourth Amended and Restated Limited Waiver extends temporary covenant relief under an existing credit agreement originally dated June 10, 2019 (as amended July 17, 2019). The transaction involves Bank of Montreal as Administrative Agent acting on behalf of Required Lenders to provide covenant waivers through November 30, 2020. **Purpose of Financing:** The waiver addresses COVID-19 pandemic impacts, specifically extending relief for: (i) financial covenant breaches under Sections 9.4.1 and 9.4.2 of the original Credit Agreement, (ii) closure default resulting from mandated casino closure exceeding 60 consecutive days, and (iii) delayed compliance certificate deliveries. **Company Background:** MGE Niagara Entertainment Inc. operates Casino Facilities under regulatory oversight. The company has been subject to government-mandated temporary closure due to COVID-19, with Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation (OLG) providing certain financial relief under the Casino Operating Services Agreement (COSA), including relief from threshold payments and continued Fixed Component Per Diem payments. --- ## 2. **INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM**

**MGE Niagara Entertainment Inc. - Fifth Amended and Restated Limited Waiver**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** November 30, 2020

**Borrower/Company Overview:** MGE Niagara Entertainment Inc., a casino operator with casino facilities subject to oversight by OLG (Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation).

**Transaction Description:** Fifth Amended and Restated Limited Waiver granted by Bank of Montreal as Administrative Agent on behalf of Required Lenders, amending and restating previous COVID-19 related waivers. The transaction involves Complex Services Inc. as guarantor and multiple lenders in a syndicated credit arrangement.

**Purpose of Financing:** The waiver extends relief from financial covenant breaches and operational defaults caused by mandatory casino facility closures due to COVID-19 pandemic restrictions. The Extended Waiver Period runs until March 31, 2021.

**Company Background and Context:** The borrower operates casino facilities under agreements with OLG and entered into the original credit agreement on June 10, 2019 (amended July 17, 2019). The company has been significantly impacted by government-mandated casino closures lasting more than 60 consecutive days due to COVID-19, resulting in financial covenant breaches and operational defaults.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths/Credit Positives:**
• OLG provides ongoing financial relief including full relief from Threshold payments and continues paying Fixed Component Per Diem to the borrower
• Borrower maintains substantial minimum liquidity requirement of $15,000,000 at all times
• Enhanced monitoring through mandatory weekly liquidity reporting with management commentary on material variations
• Pricing increases to Level 5 under the margin grid, improving lender compensation for elevated risk
• Extension fee of 5 basis points provides additional lender compensation
• Strong covenant package including restrictions on distributions, acquisitions, and material contract amendments

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• No new advances available under either credit facility during the Extended Waiver Period, limiting borrower's access to additional liquidity
• Financial covenant breaches continue through March 31, 2021, indicating ongoing operational stress
• Casino facility closure creates operational default risk if duration exceeds permitted timeframes
• New event of default triggers if OLG ceases providing Threshold payment relief or Fixed Component Per Diem payments for more than 5 business days aggregate
• Compliance certificate delivery waived through March 31, 2021, reducing financial transparency and monitoring capability
• Borrower restricted from making certain distributions, limiting financial flexibility

# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** September 6, 2024

**Borrower / Company Overview:** This joinder agreement involves multiple borrowers across the oilfield services sector, including existing borrowers Tercel Oilfield Products USA L.L.C., Pride Energy Services, LLC, and Top-Co Inc., along with new borrowers Innovex Downhole Solutions, LLC, Innovex International, Inc., and TIW Corporation.

**Transaction Description:** This is a joinder agreement to an existing Second Amended and Restated Revolving Credit, Term Loan, Guaranty and Security Agreement originally dated June 10, 2022. The transaction adds three new borrowers to the existing credit facility following a merger transaction (the "Dril-Quip Merger"). PNC Bank, National Association serves as agent, with U.S. Bank National Association identified as an additional lender based on the promissory notes referenced.

**Purpose of Financing:** The joinder adds new borrowers to an existing credit facility following a corporate merger. The agreement references that Innovex merged with and into DQ Merger Sub, LLC, with the latter surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Innovex International, Inc.

**Company Background:** The transaction involves oilfield services companies operating across multiple jurisdictions (Texas, Delaware, and Alberta). The structure indicates a consolidation within the sector, with Dril-Quip, Inc. having changed its name to Innovex International, Inc. prior to the merger completion.

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths / Credit Positives:**
• Multiple entity guarantee structure provides joint and several liability across all borrowers for enhanced credit support
• Comprehensive security package includes continuing security interests and liens on all collateral of new borrowers
• Established lending relationship with original credit agreement dating to June 10, 2022
• Pledge agreement provides additional collateral coverage through equity interests
• New borrowers become direct obligors (not sureties) under the credit agreement

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• Integration risk from adding new entities post-merger, though mitigated by comprehensive post-closing covenant requirements
• Operational complexity from multi-entity structure spanning different jurisdictions (Texas, Delaware, Alberta)
• Outstanding post-closing deliverables create execution risk, including insurance documentation, intellectual property filings, and deposit account control agreements with specific deadlines ranging from 5 to 65 days
• Potential complexity in collateral management across expanded entity base
